# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Watson_2019_fexinidazole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Watson_2019_fexinidazole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02515-18> (open access, PMC6496162)
* Supplement (NONMEM control stream, Table S1 final estimates, Stan code):
  <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02515-18>

Fexinidazole is an oral nitroimidazole for Gambian sleeping sickness (g-HAT).
It is metabolised to a sulfoxide (M1) and a slowly eliminated sulfone (M2),
which carries most of the bioactive exposure. Watson et al. fitted a
population PK model of M2 to 462 subjects and then related each subject's
cumulative exposure, summarised as the area under the natural-log M2
concentration-time curve (AUlogC), to the delayed neutropenia,
thrombocytopenia and transaminase rises seen in a dose-finding trial in
chronic Chagas disease. The packaged model carries both layers: the M2 PK
model, an `auc_log_central` state that integrates AUlogC during the solve,
and twelve four-parameter sigmoid exposure-response curves driven by that
state.

# Population

The PK model was fitted to more than 4,500 M2 concentrations from six trials
(Watson 2019 Table 1):

* phase 1 healthy male volunteers of sub-Saharan African origin in France --
  FEX001 (71; single doses of 100-3,600 mg and 14 daily doses of
  1,200-3,600 mg), FEX002 (12; food effect) and FEX003 (22; 10-day loading
  regimens);
* g-HAT patients in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African
  Republic -- FEX004 (203 adults with late-stage disease; 1,800 mg daily for
  4 days then 1,200 mg daily for 6 days) and FEX006 (114 children 6-14 years
  weighing > 20 kg, on 1,200 then 600 mg below 35 kg, and the adult regimen
  above);
* chronic indeterminate Chagas disease patients in Bolivia -- CH-FEX001 (40;
  1,200 or 1,800 mg daily for 2, 4 or 8 weeks).

156 of the 462 subjects (34%) were female. Phase 1 samples were plasma; field
samples were dried capillary blood spots (M2 blood:plasma ratio 0.97). The
twelve exposure-response curves were fitted to the 40 fexinidazole-treated
Chagas patients only.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Watson_2019_fexinidazole")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Watson_2019_fexinidazole.R`. The table collects
them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lmtt` (MTT) | log(5.65 h) | Supplement Table 1, TH1 TVMT |
| `lcl` (CL/F at 50 kg) | log(6.37 L/h) | Supplement Table 1, TH2 TVCL |
| `lvc` (V/F at 50 kg) | log(239 L) | Supplement Table 1, TH3 TVV1 |
| `lfdepot` | log(1), fixed | Supplement Table 1, TH4 TVF1 (FIX) |
| `e_dis_hat_gambiense_fdepot` | 0.956 | Supplement Table 1, TH5 TVHAT |
| `e_dis_chagas_chronic_fdepot` | 1.55 | Supplement Table 1, TH6 TVCHAGAS |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Supplement section 2.1 `$PK` (`(BW/BWMED)**(0.75)`, `**1`, `BWMED = 50`) |
| `etalmtt`, `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalfdepot` | 0.129, 0.0143, 0.0419, 0.152 | Supplement Table 1, OM1-OM4 |
| `expSd` | 0.391 | Supplement Table 1, SI1, applied as an SD (see below) |
| Depot -> 2 transits -> central, `ktr = 3 / mtt` | -- | Supplement section 2.1 (`ADVAN5`, `NN = 2`, `KTR = (NN+1)/MT`) |
| `f(depot) = exp(lfdepot + eta) * (1 + 0.956 HAT + 1.55 CHAGAS)` | -- | Supplement section 2.1 `F1 = ...` |
| `Cc ~ lnorm(expSd)` | -- | Supplement section 2.1 `$ERROR` (`Y = LOG(IPRED) + W*ERR(1)`) |
| `d/dt(auc_log_central) = log(max(Cc_nM, 1)) / 24` | -- | Methods "AUlogC to quantify drug exposure"; definition reconstructed and checked against Figure 2 (below) |
| Sigmoid outputs `e0 + emax / (1 + exp(-exp(lslope) * (AUlogC - auc50)))` | -- | Methods Eq. 1 and the supplement Stan `sigmoid()` function |
| `e0_*`, `emax_*`, `lauc50_*`, `lslope_*` | 11 curves | Digitised by the maintainers from the posterior-mean curves of Figures 4 and 7; midpoints compared with Table 2 below |
| `e0_nadir_hb` | 14.03 g/dL | Figure 7 hemoglobin nadir panel: the posterior-mean curve is flat |

# Dosing helpers

Doses are entered in micromoles of fexinidazole (MW 279.31 g/mol,
C12H13N3O3S), because the NONMEM model was fitted to molar M2 concentrations
with no scaling factor (`S2 = V1`); `Cc` is the M2 concentration in umol/L.

```{r helpers}
mw_fexinidazole <- 279.31
mg_to_umol <- function(mg) mg * 1000 / mw_fexinidazole

# One block of subjects on a once-daily regimen (`daily_mg`, one entry per
# day). Observations at time 0 and 40 days after the last dose, by which
# time M2 is far below 1 nmol/L and AUlogC has stopped accumulating.
make_regimen <- function(study, arm, n, wt, daily_mg, ghat, chagas, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  t_end <- 24 * (length(daily_mg) - 1) + 24 * 40
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, k = seq_along(daily_mg)) |>
    mutate(time = 24 * (k - 1), amt = mg_to_umol(daily_mg[k]), evid = 1L, cmt = "depot") |>
    select(-k)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = c(0, t_end)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  covs <- tibble(
    id = ids, WT = wt, DIS_HAT_GAMBIENSE = ghat, DIS_CHAGAS_CHRONIC = chagas,
    study = study, arm = arm, total_mgkg = sum(daily_mg) / wt
  )
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(covs, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ghat_adult <- c(rep(1800, 4), rep(1200, 6))
ghat_child <- c(rep(1200, 4), rep(600, 6))
```

# Typical-value exposure (AUlogC) and Figure 2

Watson 2019 does not print the AUlogC formula. The packaged model integrates
`ln(C)` with `C` in nmol/L, counts only the time the concentration is above
1 nmol/L (where `ln C > 0`), and reports the area in days. Three anchors in
the paper pin that reading down: the g-HAT cluster of Figure 2 sits at about
195, the healthy-volunteer 100 mg single doses form the floor of Figure 2 at
about 40, and the Discussion states that a total dose of about 400 mg/kg
corresponds to an AUlogC of about 300.

```{r typical-auc}
mod <- readModelDb("Watson_2019_fexinidazole")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

typ_cases <- bind_rows(
  make_regimen("g-HAT", "Adult regimen, 50 kg", 1, 50, ghat_adult, 1, 0, 0L),
  make_regimen("g-HAT", "Child regimen, 25 kg", 1, 25, ghat_child, 1, 0, 1L),
  make_regimen("Healthy volunteer", "100 mg single dose, 70 kg", 1, 70, 100, 0, 0, 2L),
  make_regimen("Healthy volunteer", "1,800/1,200 mg 10-day, 70 kg", 1, 70, ghat_adult, 0, 0, 3L),
  make_regimen("Chagas", "1,200 mg x 2 weeks, 65 kg", 1, 65, rep(1200, 14), 0, 1, 4L),
  make_regimen("Chagas", "1,200 mg x 8 weeks, 65 kg", 1, 65, rep(1200, 56), 0, 1, 5L),
  make_regimen("Chagas", "1,800 mg x 8 weeks, 65 kg", 1, 65, rep(1800, 56), 0, 1, 6L)
)
typ_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_cases, keep = c("study", "arm", "total_mgkg")) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_auc <- typ_sim |>
  group_by(id, study, arm, total_mgkg) |>
  summarise(AUlogC = max(auc_log_central), .groups = "drop")
typ_auc |>
  select(-id) |>
  mutate(total_mgkg = round(total_mgkg), AUlogC = round(AUlogC)) |>
  rename(Population = study, Regimen = arm, "Total dose (mg/kg)" = total_mgkg) |>
  knitr::kable()

auc_of <- function(lbl) {
  v <- typ_auc$AUlogC[typ_auc$arm == lbl]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique typical case '", lbl, "'")
  v
}
stopifnot(
  # Figure 2: g-HAT adults cluster at about 195.
  abs(auc_of("Adult regimen, 50 kg") - 195) < 15,
  # Figure 2: the 100 mg single doses form the floor at about 40.
  abs(auc_of("100 mg single dose, 70 kg") - 40) < 8
)
```

The ODE accumulator is checked against an independent trapezoidal
integration of the same solved concentrations on an hourly grid:

```{r trapezoid}
ev_chk <- make_regimen("g-HAT", "adult", 1, 50, ghat_adult, 1, 0, 0L) |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 24 * 60, by = 0.25), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")) |>
  mutate(WT = 50, DIS_HAT_GAMBIENSE = 1, DIS_CHAGAS_CHRONIC = 0) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
chk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_chk) |> as.data.frame()
y <- pmax(0, log(pmax(chk$Cc * 1000, 1e-300)))
trap <- sum(diff(chk$time) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2) / 24
c(ode = max(chk$auc_log_central), trapezoid = trap)
stopifnot(abs(max(chk$auc_log_central) / trap - 1) < 0.005)
```

To place the 400 mg/kg anchor, a 65 kg Chagas patient is given 1,200 mg
daily for increasing numbers of days:

```{r threshold}
n_days <- c(7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 56)
thr_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(n_days), function(i) {
  make_regimen("Chagas", paste(n_days[i], "days"), 1, 65, rep(1200, n_days[i]), 0, 1, i)
}))
thr <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = thr_ev, keep = c("arm", "total_mgkg")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  group_by(arm, total_mgkg) |>
  summarise(AUlogC = max(auc_log_central), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(total_mgkg)
mgkg_at_300 <- approx(thr$AUlogC, thr$total_mgkg, xout = 300)$y
thr |> mutate(across(c(total_mgkg, AUlogC), round)) |> knitr::kable()
round(mgkg_at_300)
stopifnot(mgkg_at_300 > 300, mgkg_at_300 < 500)
```

# Virtual cohort and Figure 2

The cohort approximates the six trials of Figure 2 with the body-weight
distributions of its right-hand panels. FEX002 (a three-period food-effect
crossover) is omitted because its per-period doses are not reported.

```{r cohort}
# Seeds rxode2's own RNG for the between-subject draws. The draw is
# reproducible for a given rxode2 build and thread count, not across them,
# so every assertion below is on a median of many subjects.
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
clamp <- function(x, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)
wt_hv <- function(n) clamp(rnorm(n, 72, 9), 55, 98)

sd_levels <- c(100, 200, 400, 600, 1200, 1800, 2400, 3600)
blocks <- list()
off <- 0L
for (d in sd_levels) {
  blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("Healthy volunteers (FEX001)", paste(d, "mg single"), 7, wt_hv(7), d, 0, 0, off)
  off <- off + 7L
}
for (d in c(1200, 2400, 3600)) {
  blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("Healthy volunteers (FEX001)", paste(d, "mg x 14 d"), 6, wt_hv(6), rep(d, 14), 0, 0, off)
  off <- off + 6L
}
blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("Healthy volunteers (FEX003)", "1,800/1,200 mg", 11, wt_hv(11), ghat_adult, 0, 0, off)
off <- off + 11L
blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("Healthy volunteers (FEX003)", "2,400/1,200 mg", 11, wt_hv(11), c(rep(2400, 4), rep(1200, 6)), 0, 0, off)
off <- off + 11L
blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("g-HAT (FEX004)", "adult regimen", 150, clamp(rnorm(150, 50, 9), 30, 75), ghat_adult, 1, 0, off)
off <- off + 150L
blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("g-HAT (FEX006)", "child regimen", 60, runif(60, 20, 35), ghat_child, 1, 0, off)
off <- off + 60L
for (d in c(1200, 1800)) {
  for (w in c(2, 4, 8)) {
    blocks[[length(blocks) + 1]] <- make_regimen("Chagas (CH-FEX001)", paste0(d, " mg x ", w, " wk"), 7, clamp(rnorm(7, 66, 10), 45, 105), rep(d, 7 * w), 0, 1, off)
    off <- off + 7L
  }
}
cohort <- bind_rows(blocks)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(distinct(cohort, id, study, arm)$id))
nrow(distinct(cohort, id))
```

```{r cohort-sim}
cohort_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = cohort, keep = c("study", "arm", "total_mgkg")) |>
  as.data.frame()
cohort_auc <- cohort_sim |>
  group_by(id, study, arm, total_mgkg) |>
  summarise(AUlogC = max(auc_log_central), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(cohort_auc, aes(total_mgkg, AUlogC, colour = study, shape = study)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 300, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 400, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Healthy volunteers (FEX001)" = "#E66100", "Healthy volunteers (FEX003)" = "#F5C26B",
    "g-HAT (FEX004)" = "#1B7837", "g-HAT (FEX006)" = "#7FBF7B",
    "Chagas (CH-FEX001)" = "#D01C8B"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "Total mg/kg dose", y = "AUlogC of fexinidazole sulfone",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 (left) of Watson 2019 with a simulated cohort."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-2-check}
fig2 <- cohort_auc |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(), median_mgkg = median(total_mgkg),
    AUlogC_p05 = quantile(AUlogC, 0.05), AUlogC_median = median(AUlogC),
    AUlogC_p95 = quantile(AUlogC, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )
fig2 |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round)) |> knitr::kable()
med_of <- function(s) {
  v <- fig2$AUlogC_median[fig2$study == s]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no study '", s, "'")
  v
}
stopifnot(
  # Figure 2: the FEX004 adults sit between about 150 and 230, centred near 195.
  abs(med_of("g-HAT (FEX004)") - 195) < 20,
  # Figure 2: the FEX006 children sit slightly below the adults.
  med_of("g-HAT (FEX006)") < med_of("g-HAT (FEX004)") + 5
)
```

The g-HAT clusters, the healthy-volunteer floor near 40 and the Chagas
patients climbing past 300 above about 400 mg/kg match Figure 2. Two
differences remain, and neither was tuned away:

* **Chagas patients reach higher doses here than in the trial.** CH-FEX001
  was interrupted after the toxicity signal, so most patients took less than
  their planned course (Table 1: median 251 mg/kg, range 61-1,400). The
  cohort here gives every patient the full planned course, so its 8-week
  arms extend to about 1,500 mg/kg and an AUlogC of about 750, beyond the
  1,400 mg/kg and 660 maximum of Figure 2. Below about 1,000 mg/kg the
  simulated Chagas points follow the trend of the observed ones.
* **Healthy volunteers on high or repeated doses sit below Figure 2.** The
  typical 72 kg volunteer on 1,200-3,600 mg daily for 14 days (FEX001 part 3,
  233-700 mg/kg) reaches an AUlogC of 220-254, whereas the corresponding
  Figure 2 triangles lie at about 260-310; likewise the 3,600 mg single dose
  gives 97 against a single-dose cluster that reaches about 150. The g-HAT
  and low-dose anchors are matched, and the packaged PK model has no
  study-specific term for the phase 1 volunteers beyond the shared
  relative-bioavailability reference, so the gap is most likely carried by
  those volunteers' individual (post hoc) random effects, which the paper
  used to compute AUlogC and does not report. It is also possible that the
  unprinted AUlogC definition differs from the reconstruction in a way that
  only matters for long exposures in volunteers; see Assumptions and
  deviations.

# Typical M2 concentration-time profiles

Figure 1 of the paper shows conditionally weighted residuals rather than a
concentration profile, so there is no published profile to overlay. The
typical profiles below show the effect of the population-specific relative
bioavailability on the g-HAT adult regimen.

```{r profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
prof_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  tibble(id = i, time = 24 * (0:9), amt = mg_to_umol(ghat_adult), evid = 1L, cmt = "depot") |>
    bind_rows(tibble(id = i, time = seq(0, 24 * 20, by = 1), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central"))
})) |>
  mutate(
    WT = 50,
    population = c("Healthy volunteer", "g-HAT patient", "Chagas patient")[id],
    DIS_HAT_GAMBIENSE = as.numeric(id == 2), DIS_CHAGAS_CHRONIC = as.numeric(id == 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
prof <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = prof_ev, keep = "population") |> as.data.frame()
ggplot(prof, aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = population)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "M2 concentration (umol/L)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical 50 kg subject, 1,800 mg daily x 4 days then 1,200 mg daily x 6 days."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Exposure-response curves (Figures 4 and 7)

The twelve sigmoid outputs are algebraic functions of the `auc_log_central`
state. To trace each curve over the published exposure range, the state is
set directly by a bolus of the desired AUlogC into `auc_log_central` with no
drug given, so the accumulator holds that value and every output is
evaluated at it.

```{r er-grid}
er_x <- seq(0, 700, by = 5)
er_grid <- tibble(id = seq_along(er_x), x = er_x)
er_ev <- bind_rows(
  mutate(er_grid, time = 0, amt = x, evid = 1L, cmt = "auc_log_central"),
  mutate(er_grid, time = 1, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  select(-x) |>
  mutate(WT = 65, DIS_HAT_GAMBIENSE = 0, DIS_CHAGAS_CHRONIC = 1) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
er_out <- c(
  "log10_peak_alt", "log2_peak_alt_fold", "log10_peak_ast", "log2_peak_ast_fold",
  "nadir_neutrophil_count", "nadir_neutrophil_pct_change",
  "nadir_platelet_count", "nadir_platelet_pct_change",
  "nadir_lymphocyte_count", "nadir_lymphocyte_pct_change",
  "nadir_hb", "nadir_hb_pct_change"
)
er <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = er_ev) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(AUlogC = auc_log_central, all_of(er_out)) |>
  pivot_longer(-AUlogC, names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(output = factor(output, levels = er_out))
stopifnot(abs(range(er$AUlogC) - c(0, 700)) < 1e-6)
```

The reference points below were read by the maintainers from the
posterior-mean (thick) curves of Figures 4 and 7 at fixed AUlogC values. The
model parameters were fitted to the full digitised curves, so the comparison
confirms the transcription (sign, scale and orientation of every curve)
rather than providing independent validation.

```{r er-reference}
er_ref <- tribble(
  ~output, ~AUlogC, ~value,
  "log10_peak_alt", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(1.558, 1.659, 1.889, 2.137, 2.263, 2.313),
  "log2_peak_alt_fold", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(0.7045, 1.195, 1.864, 2.573, 3.186, 3.718),
  "log10_peak_ast", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(1.542, 1.562, 1.682, 1.977, 2.127, 2.157),
  "log2_peak_ast_fold", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(0.7627, 0.7849, 0.9956, 1.905, 2.869, 3.113),
  "nadir_neutrophil_count", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(2.298, 2.269, 1.865, 0.8558, 0.5096, 0.4808),
  "nadir_neutrophil_pct_change", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(7.379, 6.214, -8.932, -34.56, -38.06, -38.06),
  "nadir_platelet_count", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(238.3, 225.9, 205.2, 178.3, 153.4, 134.8),
  "nadir_platelet_pct_change", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(-11.72, -12.66, -36.09, -42.66, -42.66, -42.66),
  "nadir_lymphocyte_count", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(1.457, 1.47, 1.443, 1.43, 1.43, 1.404),
  "nadir_lymphocyte_pct_change", c(50, 150, 350, 450, 600), c(-20.56, -20.98, -36.5, -36.92, -36.92),
  "nadir_hb", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(14.06, 14.06, 14.06, 13.97, 14.01, 14.01),
  "nadir_hb_pct_change", c(50, 150, 250, 350, 450, 600), c(-8.908, -8.908, -9.916, -12.61, -13.78, -13.95)
) |>
  unnest(c(AUlogC, value)) |>
  mutate(output = factor(output, levels = er_out))

model_at <- function(out, x) {
  d <- er[er$output == out, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0L) stop("no model curve for '", out, "'")
  approx(d$AUlogC, d$value, xout = x)$y
}
er_cmp <- er_ref |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(model = model_at(as.character(output), AUlogC)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(output) |>
  mutate(panel_span = max(value) - min(value) + 1e-9)
er_cmp |>
  group_by(output) |>
  summarise(max_abs_diff = max(abs(model - value)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(max_abs_diff = signif(max_abs_diff, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Each curve agrees with its digitised reference to well within one plotting
# line width (2% of the figure's y-axis range is a few pixels).
y_axis_span <- c(
  log10_peak_alt = 1.5, log2_peak_alt_fold = 6, log10_peak_ast = 1.2, log2_peak_ast_fold = 5,
  nadir_neutrophil_count = 3, nadir_neutrophil_pct_change = 120,
  nadir_platelet_count = 300, nadir_platelet_pct_change = 60,
  nadir_lymphocyte_count = 1.5, nadir_lymphocyte_pct_change = 60,
  nadir_hb = 6, nadir_hb_pct_change = 20
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(er_cmp) == 71,
  all(abs(er_cmp$model - er_cmp$value) / y_axis_span[as.character(er_cmp$output)] < 0.02)
)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
ghat_band <- cohort_auc |>
  filter(grepl("g-HAT", study)) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(AUlogC, 0.05), hi = quantile(AUlogC, 0.95))
liver <- c("log10_peak_alt", "log2_peak_alt_fold", "log10_peak_ast", "log2_peak_ast_fold")
ggplot(filter(er, output %in% liver), aes(AUlogC, value)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = ghat_band$lo, xmax = ghat_band$hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#7FBF7B", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = filter(er_ref, output %in% liver), colour = "#D01C8B") +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Cumulative M2 AUlogC", y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the posterior-mean curves of Figure 4 of Watson 2019 (line: model;",
      "points: digitised curve). Shading: 5th-95th percentile of simulated g-HAT AUlogC."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-7, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 9}
heme <- setdiff(er_out, liver)
ggplot(filter(er, output %in% heme), aes(AUlogC, value)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = ghat_band$lo, xmax = ghat_band$hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#7FBF7B", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = filter(er_ref, output %in% heme), colour = "#D01C8B") +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Cumulative M2 AUlogC", y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the posterior-mean curves of Figure 7 of Watson 2019 (line: model;",
      "points: digitised curve). Shading: 5th-95th percentile of simulated g-HAT AUlogC."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The green bands of Figures 4 and 7 span roughly 150-190; the simulated g-HAT
range here is `r round(ghat_band$lo)`-`r round(ghat_band$hi)`, consistent
with the spread of the g-HAT points in Figure 2.

## Midpoints against Table 2

Table 2 gives only the 80% credible interval of each EC50 (the `auc50`
midpoint). The digitised curves place 10 of the 11 fitted midpoints inside
those intervals:

```{r table-2}
theta <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta
tab2 <- tribble(
  ~output, ~ci_lo, ~ci_hi,
  "nadir_neutrophil_count", 262, 342,
  "nadir_neutrophil_pct_change", 208, 352,
  "nadir_platelet_count", 146, 240,
  "nadir_platelet_pct_change", 199, 240,
  "nadir_lymphocyte_count", 74, 1304,
  "nadir_lymphocyte_pct_change", 163, 396,
  "nadir_hb_pct_change", 137, 842,
  "log10_peak_alt", 164, 362,
  "log2_peak_alt_fold", 119, 371,
  "log10_peak_ast", 244, 371,
  "log2_peak_ast_fold", 256, 396
) |>
  mutate(
    auc50 = exp(unname(theta[paste0("lauc50_", output)])),
    inside = auc50 >= ci_lo & auc50 <= ci_hi
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(tab2$auc50))
tab2 |>
  mutate(auc50 = round(auc50)) |>
  rename(Output = output, "Table 2 CI80 low" = ci_lo, "Table 2 CI80 high" = ci_hi, "Model auc50" = auc50, "Inside CI80" = inside) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  sum(tab2$inside) == 10,
  !tab2$inside[tab2$output == "nadir_platelet_count"]
)
```

The absolute platelet model is the exception: its plotted posterior-mean
curve falls gently across the whole exposure range, and the sigmoid that
reproduces that mean curve has its midpoint at about 311, above the
146-240 credible interval. A posterior-mean curve averages sigmoids with
different midpoints, which flattens it, so its apparent midpoint need not
lie within the marginal credible interval of the midpoint parameter. The
packaged curve follows the published mean curve. The hemoglobin nadir
curve is flat, so its midpoint is not identifiable and the output is a
constant; Table 2 gives a 73-1,383 interval with a 75% overlap coefficient,
i.e. no exposure effect.

## Predictions for the g-HAT regimen

The Results apply the relative models to exposures distributed as in the
g-HAT trials. The typical curves evaluated over the simulated g-HAT cohort
give:

```{r ghat-predictions}
ghat_auc <- cohort_auc$AUlogC[grepl("g-HAT", cohort_auc$study)]
pred <- tibble(
  Outcome = c(
    "Neutrophil nadir change (%)", "Platelet nadir change (%)",
    "Peak ALT fold change", "Peak AST fold change"
  ),
  Model = c(
    median(model_at("nadir_neutrophil_pct_change", ghat_auc)),
    median(model_at("nadir_platelet_pct_change", ghat_auc)),
    median(2^model_at("log2_peak_alt_fold", ghat_auc)),
    median(2^model_at("log2_peak_ast_fold", ghat_auc))
  ),
  Paper = c(0, -20, 2.8, 2.0),
  `Paper statement` = c(
    "median relative decrease of 0%",
    "median decrease of 20%",
    "50% would have ALT > 2.8 x baseline",
    "50% would have AST > 2 x baseline"
  )
)
pred |> mutate(Model = signif(Model, 3)) |> knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  abs(pred$Model[1] - 0) < 8,
  abs(pred$Model[2] - (-20)) < 5,
  abs(pred$Model[3] - 2.8) < 0.5
)
```

Neutrophils, platelets and ALT reproduce the published predictions. The
typical AST fold change is lower than the paper's "more than 2 times" for
half the g-HAT patients: the posterior-mean AST curve of Figure 4 is still
near its baseline in the g-HAT exposure range, so the paper's statement must
draw on the posterior predictive spread (parameter uncertainty and residual
error), which the typical curve does not carry.

# PKNCA check of the PK layer

Watson 2019 reports no non-compartmental summary of M2, so the PKNCA check
is against the model's own closed form: for a typical subject after a single
dose, AUC0-inf must equal `F * Dose / CL` and the terminal half-life
`ln(2) * V / CL`.

```{r pknca-typical}
nca_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(600, 1200, 1800)), function(i) {
  d <- c(600, 1200, 1800)[i]
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = i, time = 0, amt = mg_to_umol(d), evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(id = i, time = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168, 216, 264, 336), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(d, "mg"))
})) |>
  mutate(WT = 70, DIS_HAT_GAMBIENSE = 0, DIS_CHAGAS_CHRONIC = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
nca_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = nca_ev, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()

conc_df <- nca_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_df <- bind_rows(conc_df, conc_df |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)
dose_df <- nca_ev |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

cl_70 <- 6.37 * (70 / 50)^0.75
v_70 <- 239 * (70 / 50)
nca_wide <- nca_wide |>
  mutate(
    dose_umol = mg_to_umol(as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment))),
    auc_closed = dose_umol / cl_70,
    thalf_closed = log(2) * v_70 / cl_70
  )
nca_wide |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, auc_closed, half.life, thalf_closed) |>
  rename(
    Dose = treatment, "Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (umol*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "F*Dose/CL" = auc_closed,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life, "ln(2)*V/CL" = thalf_closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_wide) == 3,
  all(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / nca_wide$auc_closed - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(nca_wide$half.life / nca_wide$thalf_closed - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

The Results text quotes a clearance of 3 L/h, a volume of 80 L and 14% IIV
on the mean transit time, which disagree with supplement Table S1
(6.37 L/h, 239 L, 36%). The model follows Table S1 and the NONMEM control
stream, whose `$THETA` initial values (6.35 and 238) match it.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Molar units.** The NONMEM model compares `log(A(2)/V1)` with the
  natural log of the molar M2 concentration, so doses are in umol of
  fexinidazole (MW 279.31) and `Cc` is M2 in umol/L. The unit was confirmed
  by reproducing the AUlogC values of Figure 2.
* **Residual error.** The `$ERROR` block multiplies `ERR(1) ~ N(0, SIGMA)`
  by `W = SQRT(SIGMA(1,1))`, so the SD of log concentration is SIGMA itself,
  0.391, not its square root. `expSd = 0.391`.
* **Results text vs Table S1.** Where the Results text (CL 3 L/h, V 80 L)
  disagrees with Table S1 and the code (6.37 L/h, 239 L), the model follows
  Table S1 and the code.
* **AUlogC definition.** Not printed. Reconstructed as the integral of
  `max(0, ln C)` with `C` in nmol/L and time in days, which reproduces the
  three anchors of Figure 2 and the Discussion (above). Other readings
  (umol/L, pmol/L, hours, or no truncation) miss them by large factors. It
  underpredicts the Figure 2 values of the FEX001 multiple-dose volunteers by
  15-20% (typical 220-254 against about 260-310).
* **Exposure-response parameters from figures.** The posterior summaries of
  the Bayesian fits were not printed beyond the 80% credible intervals of
  EC50 (Table 2). Every `e0`, `emax`, `lauc50` and `lslope` was obtained by
  the maintainers by fitting the four-parameter sigmoid to the posterior-mean
  curve digitised from Figure 4 or 7 (230-280 points per panel; root mean
  squared error under one pixel). These parameters describe the mean curve,
  not the posterior mean of each parameter.
* **Absolute platelet midpoint outside Table 2.** See the Table 2 section:
  311 versus a credible interval of 146-240, a consequence of matching the
  flattened posterior-mean curve.
* **Hemoglobin nadir** is encoded as the constant 14.03 g/dL, the flat
  posterior-mean curve of Figure 7.
* **No residual error on the exposure-response outputs.** The 90% posterior
  prediction bands of Figures 4 and 7 combine parameter uncertainty with the
  residual SD, and the residual SDs themselves are not reported, so the
  outputs are typical-value predictions. For simulation the absolute models
  used a log-normal error and the relative models an additive normal error
  (Methods, supplement Stan code).
* **`e0` is the low-exposure asymptote**, the Stan `max_effect`, not the
  value at zero exposure; the two differ by less than 3% of `emax` for every
  curve except absolute lymphocytes (13%), ALT fold change (12%) and
  absolute platelets (4%).
* **Scope of the exposure-response curves.** They were fitted to 40 chronic
  Chagas patients, and the paper shows that the liver curves overpredict
  transaminase rises in g-HAT patients. Each output is a per-subject summary
  (nadir or peak over follow-up) of the cumulative AUlogC at the end of
  treatment, so only its value after M2 has been eliminated is meaningful.
* **Virtual cohort.** Body weights follow the histograms of Figure 2; FEX002
  is omitted because its per-period doses are not reported.
